name: Tarlatamab
mechanism: Half-life-extended bispecific T-cell engager binding DLL3 on SCLC cells and CD3 on T cells, forming a cytolytic synapse and redirecting polyclonal T cells to kill DLL3-expressing tumour cells independent of MHC presentation.
keyToxicities: Cytokine release syndrome (mostly during step-up dosing)
Immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS) and other neurological toxicity
monitoring: Step-up dosing with close monitoring (including observation in a suitable facility) after initial doses
Vital signs and neurological assessment for CRS and ICANS
Blood counts and liver function tests
Patient education on CRS/ICANS symptoms and driving restrictions
interactions: Cytokine release may transiently suppress CYP450 enzymes, affecting narrow-therapeutic-index co-medications.
resistance: Loss or downregulation of DLL3 with lineage plasticity, T-cell exhaustion and immunosuppressive microenvironment.
